jobs.title: Environmental and Radioactive Waste Management Program Manager
jobs.location: Paducah, KY or Los Angeles, CA
jobs.description:
About the Company

General Matter is enriching uranium in America.

Our goal is to design, build, and operate the world’s lowest-cost enrichment services in the United States.

Our mission is to restore America’s ability to produce nuclear fuel—fuel that will power AI, advanced manufacturing, critical industries, and the next generation of nuclear reactors.

Ultimately, our work will help power national ambitions and enable a high-energy society.

We were incubated by Founders Fund, like Anduril and Palantir before us, and are backed by top-tier investors. Our lean, world-class team of engineers and operators is applying a first-principles approach to solving the problem of nuclear fuel production.

We are a mission-driven company with a culture of urgency, accountability, and transparency.

Help us build a high-energy society by making the cleanest, safest form of baseload energy the most affordable.

About This Role

The Environmental and Waste Management Program Manager builds and owns General Matter's environmental protection and radioactive waste management program — the function responsible for protecting the public and the environment from facility operations under applicable nuclear regulation, distinct from General Matter's broader environmental health and safety function. This role establishes the permits, procedures, and monitoring systems required to ensure compliance with NRC, DOE, and international standards (e.g., 10 CFR Part 20, ICRP, and ANSI), and manages the full lifecycle of radioactive waste from characterization through disposition. The role operates independently of production activities, with the authority to halt operations that pose a risk to the environment or public health.

Responsibilities

- Identify environmental obligations imposed by applicable federal, state, and local regulations

- Establish and maintain the environmental monitoring program

- Secure and maintain the permits, licenses, and registrations required for radiological and non-radiological discharges, and for waste handling and disposal

- Review and approve operations, and proposed changes to operations, that carry potential for environmental release

- Develop the criteria, procedures, and training used to monitor gaseous and liquid effluents

- Establish and manage the facility's radioactive waste management program, including waste minimization consistent with 10 CFR 20.1406 and the safe handling, storage, and disposition of solid and liquid radioactive waste

- Characterize waste generation and identify opportunities to reduce waste volume and contamination, and manage waste to facilitate eventual decommissioning

- Verify ongoing compliance with environmental and waste management requirements through inspections and audits

- Exercise independent authority to halt operations that may pose a risk to the environment or public health

- Build the program's processes, procedures, and infrastructure largely from the ground up

Basic Qualifications

- B.S. or B.A. in a science or engineering discipline with 8+ years of relevant experience in environmental protection, waste management, or applied health physics, including 3+ years in a nuclear/radiological setting; OR advanced degree (M.S. or Ph.D.) in a science or engineering discipline with 5+ years of relevant experience, including 3+ years in a nuclear/radiological setting

- Ability to obtain and maintain required security clearance and access authorization

Preferred Skills and Experience

- Prior experience at an NRC-licensed facility, DOE site, or national laboratory

- Professional certification such as Registered Environmental Manager (REM), Certified Safety Professional (CSP), or Associate Safety Professional (ASP)

- Experience managing radiological and hazardous waste programs

- Experience building or managing a small team

- Experience operating in a fast-paced, resource-constrained, or startup environment

Additional Requirements

Ability to work extended hours and weekends as necessary.

Equal Opportunity Employer

General Matter is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with General Matter is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.

Compensation and Benefits

The base salary range for this role is $130,000–$190,000 annually.

Compensation bands are determined by role, level, location, and alignment with market data. Individual level and base pay is determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on job-related skills, education, experience, technical capabilities and internal equity. Please note that the stated salary range is an estimate and may be adjusted based on market conditions, business needs, or other factors. In addition to base salary, for full-time hires, you may also be eligible for long-term incentives, in the form of stock options, and access to medical, vision & dental coverage as well as access to a 401(k) retirement plan.

jobs.description:
About the Company

General Matter enriches uranium.

We are designing, building, and operating the world's lowest-cost enrichment services, here in the US.

In the process, we are restoring America's ability to produce nuclear fuel to power AI, advanced manufacturing and critical industries our country relies on to remain competitive.

Fuel drives the cost of advanced reactor electricity production, and enrichment drives the cost of the fuel that advanced reactors consume. Reliable, low-cost enrichment is the catalyst for the nuclear Renaissance now under way.

Our mission is to make nuclear not only the cleanest and safest source of baseload power, but also the most affordable. We believe abundant nuclear energy will lead to a post-scarcity society.

We are a mission-driven company with a culture of urgency, accountability, and transparency.

Help us build a high-energy society by making the cleanest, safest form of baseload energy the most affordable.

About This Role

As Contingent Workforce Program Manager at General Matter, you'll own our contingent workforce program end to end and build the systems that let it scale. You'll design how General Matter finds, contracts, onboards, and manages every 1099 independent contractor, LLC's, advisors,W-2 2 staffing agencies, and subcontracting vendors. You will own the process end-to-end, from building a vetted supplier base and negotiating competitive terms to partnering with Procurement, Legal, and Finance to streamline workflows, coordinating access controls with IT, managing onboarding, overseeing active agreements and renewals, and ensuring seamless offboarding. This is a high-ownership role for an operator who carries work from start to finish with no loose ends, escalates quickly and appropriately, and wants to grow the program as the business scales. If you seek high impact and are excited by fast-paced, intense, Skunkworks-style projects, we encourage you to apply to join our team.

Responsibilities

- Own the contingent workforce program end to end, from intake and approval through sourcing, contracting, onboarding, and offboarding.

- Build scalable, end-to-end processes for 1099 contractors, LLCs, temp staffing agencies, and subcontracting vendors, including classification guidelines and co-employment safeguards.

- Build and manage General Matter's supplier base, and negotiate rates and terms in partnership with Procurement, Legal, and Finance as you take ownership of SOW and subcontractor engagements.

- Define what access each contractor needs and put controls in place, including export-control compliance and clearance requirements, without slowing the business down.

- Set requirements for construction and site subcontractors, including liability insurance and certificates of insurance, and resolve edge cases.

- Establish program health measures and operational insights that identify systemic issues, inform priorities, and drive measurable improvements in service, efficiency, adoption, supplier performance, and risk.

- Use automation and AI tools to build, scale, and automate intake, tracking, and reporting as request volume grows.

- Partner with People, Legal, Finance, Security, and IT to run a large, cross-functional program, and escalate issues quickly with clear recommendations.

Basic Qualifications

- 6-10 years of experience in contingent workforce, extended workforce, procurement operations, vendor management, or HR operations.

- Experience at a fast-paced tech startup that went through meaningful scale, including building processes to handle a rising volume of contractor requests.

- Hands-on experience managing SOW and subcontractor engagements, including sourcing suppliers and negotiating terms.

- Strong working knowledge of worker classification, co-employment, and contractor compliance.

- Experience using automation and AI tools to scale operational processes.

- A track record of owning large, cross-functional programs end to end, with sound judgment about when and how to escalate

Preferred Skills and Experience

- Experience building a contingent workforce program from the ground up at a fast-growing startup, ideally within hard tech.

- Experience managing construction or site contractor programs, including subcontractor insurance and site onboarding.

- Demonstrated ability to own complex programs end to end across interdisciplinary teams, coordinating competing priorities, driving decisions, and delivering results with no loose ends.

- Scaling an extended workforce program at a high-growth company with both exempt and non-exempt populations.

- Experienced partnering with employer-of-record providers.

Ability to work extended hours and weekends as necessary.

Procurement & Sourcing (Primary Focus)

- Source and qualify suppliers for mechanical, electrical, and specialty hardware components.

- Lead RFQs, negotiate pricing/terms, and drive cost-down initiatives.

- Build and maintain a preferred vendor list and category strategies.

- Manage supplier performance metrics: on-time delivery, quality, responsiveness, and risk.

- Proactively identify and mitigate supply risks or single-source vulnerabilities.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

- Partner with engineering to define BOMs, establish part specifications, and forecast component needs.

- Work with manufacturing and operations teams to support build schedules and ensure material readiness.

- Coordinate with finance on budgeting, cash-flow implications, and cost forecasts.

Systems & Infrastructure

- Set up foundational tools (ERP/MRP, purchasing workflows, inventory management).

- Establish documentation standards for procurement, supplier onboarding, and quality tracking.

- Drive continuous improvement across the supply chain to increase transparency and efficiency.

Basic Qualifications

- 4–8+ years of supply chain, procurement, or sourcing experience—preferably in hardware, devices, or manufacturing environments.

- Proven experience owning procurement strategies and negotiating with suppliers.

- Strong understanding of hardware development cycles (prototype → pilot → production).

- Ability to manage competing priorities in a fast-paced, resource-constrained startup environment.

- Analytical mindset with comfort working in spreadsheets, ERP/MRP systems, and BOM tools.

- Excellent communication and relationship-building skills—internally and externally.

- Bias toward action; willingness to dive into the details and do the unglamorous work when needed.

Preferred Skills and Experience

- Experience setting up or optimizing ERP/MRP systems in a startup environment.

- Familiarity with global logistics, customs, and compliance.

General Matter enriches uranium.

About This Role

General Matter is building the enrichment capacity America needs to produce its own nuclear fuel, and every dollar we spend getting there has to count. We are looking for a Financial Analyst to run the day-to-day finance operations that keep our engineers and operators moving: leading our accounts payable program, owning our procure-to-pay and spend platform, and building the reports that show leadership where the money is going and how it tracks against plan. You will also help build the budgets, cost models, and long-range projections behind the company’s biggest decisions, and at times embed directly with engineering teams during major development campaigns. If you want real ownership early in your career and a direct view into how a hard-tech company gets funded and built, this role is for you.

Responsibilities

- Lead the accounts payable program day to day. Process and approve vendor invoices, keep payments on time, and resolve issues with suppliers and internal teams.

- Own the procure-to-pay, card spend, and expense platform. Build the tools, workflows, and controls that keep spend visible and compliant as the company scales.

- Produce weekly reporting on spending patterns and budget-to-actuals, and flag variances to budget owners and leadership before they become problems.

- Build department and company spend projections for the annual budget and ongoing forecast cycles.

- Support strategic projects with cost modeling and analysis, including major capital programs, facility build-out, and long-range planning.

- Partner with engineering and operations teams to understand current and future needs, turn that into analysis leadership can act on, and embed with teams during major development campaigns.

Basic Qualifications

- Strong understanding of engineering fundamentals.

- Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field.

- 0–3 years of experience in finance, accounting, FP&A, or a related analytical role (internships included).

Preferred Skills and Experience

- Experience in a fast-paced engineering or highly technical environment, with a resourceful approach to delivering under tight timelines or budget constraints.

- Hands-on experience with an ERP, procure-to-pay, or spend management platform (e.g., Ramp, NetSuite, Oracle, SAP).

- Exposure to accounts payable, expense management, or month-end close processes.

- Advanced Excel skills, including building financial models, forecasts, and variance analysis from scratch.

- Ability to explain financial terms and tradeoffs clearly to engineers and other non-finance teams.

- Familiarity with SQL, Power BI, Tableau, or similar tools for automating reporting. CPA or CMA progress is a plus.

- Ability to work extended hours and weekends as necessary.

Help us build a high-energy society by making the cleanest, safest form of baseload energy the most affordable.

About This Role

General Matter is seeking an IT Procurement Specialist to own purchasing for the technology that supports our engineering teams, facilities, and business operations. You will source hardware, software, and services for corporate and security-sensitive environments, working closely with IT, Information Security, Engineering, Finance, and Supply Chain.

This is a hands-on role for someone who can turn technical requirements into accurate orders, negotiate effectively, and get critical equipment delivered on schedule. You should be comfortable challenging a quote, chasing a delayed shipment, and building purchasing processes that keep pace with a rapidly growing company without compromising security or financial discipline.

Responsibilities

- Own procurement of computers, servers, storage, networking equipment, software, and IT services, from initial request and competitive sourcing through purchase order, delivery, and invoice reconciliation.

- Partner with technical teams to validate specifications and configurations, forecast demand, and secure long-lead equipment ahead of hiring, facility buildouts, and deployment milestones.

- Build relationships with manufacturers and authorized resellers; negotiate pricing, delivery commitments, licensing, warranties, and support terms while balancing cost, schedule, and supplier risk.

- Coordinate with Information Security and Legal to complete required reviews before purchase, use approved sourcing channels, verify equipment provenance, and prevent unauthorized substitutions or disclosure of sensitive information.

- Track open orders, expedite critical shipments, resolve receiving discrepancies, and coordinate equipment handoff to IT with accurate purchasing, serial-number, and warranty records.

- Manage software and support renewals, track spending and license entitlements, and improve purchasing workflows to reduce delays, eliminate unnecessary costs, and maintain clear ownership and audit-ready records.

Basic Qualifications

- 3+ years of experience in IT procurement, technical purchasing, or technology vendor management, including direct responsibility for hardware and software purchases.

- Working knowledge of enterprise IT equipment, software licensing, and support contracts, with the ability to review technical bills of materials and identify missing or inconsistent quote details.

- Demonstrated ability to negotiate commercial terms, hold suppliers accountable, and resolve delivery or purchasing issues without constant oversight.

- Experience using purchasing or ERP systems and spreadsheets to manage purchase orders, spending, delivery schedules, and renewals.

- Strong attention to detail, clear communication, and sound judgment when handling sensitive information and competing priorities.

Preferred Skills and Experience

- Procurement experience in aerospace, defense, nuclear, or other security-sensitive engineering environments.

- Experience supporting classified or export-controlled programs, including supplier qualification, supply-chain traceability, and controlled receiving requirements.

- Familiarity with software licensing, offline activation, and vendor-support restrictions in isolated or air-gapped environments.

- Experience purchasing data-center infrastructure and negotiating with enterprise hardware manufacturers, software publishers, and value-added resellers.

- Experience building practical, scalable purchasing processes at a fast-growing company or supporting simultaneous deployments across multiple facilities.

Additional Requirements

- Ability to work extended hours and weekends as necessary.

- Ability to come into our office every day. This role is 100% on site and in person.

- Currently a US Citizen with capability to obtain and maintain a US Q clearance.

Equal Opportunity Employer
